reviewer_evidence.full_rule_simulation: Scratchpad only; no project file touched. Real hg19 predictor (5,225 finite tiles); synthetic PC1 per sample = -z(baseline lamina) + 0.55*AR(0.9) shared structure + per-replicate noise (SD 0.15; KO rep2 SD 0.30 for the half-depth sample) + KO shift -beta*z(dlam); each track unit-scaled per chromosome exactly as pc1.compartment_eigenvector does; frozen evaluator through replicate.adapter_registration with 299 shifts; all four cross pairs; 12 seeds per level. Results: eligible tiles ~4,600 (chr4, chr10 excluded by the 0.2 orientation floor in this synthetic model; genome orientation rho 0.40). beta=0: tier A 0/12, tier B 0/12, four-pairs-all-negative 2/12, ratio component 3/12, no effect or p component passed. Realised unadjusted rho -0.048 (SD 0.014): tier A 5/12 (unadjusted effect 5, standardised effect 5, adjusted effect 11, pairs 11). rho -0.085: tier A 12/12, tier B 5/12 (adjusted mean -0.101). rho -0.107: tier A 12/12, tier B 12/12. rho -0.156 and -0.212: 12/12.
reviewer_evidence.amplitude_adversarial: No effect, KO amplitude x1.25 before unit scaling, 6 seeds: unadjusted rho -0.011..+0.021, no component passed; genome SD ratio 0.996-0.998 (the scaling in pc1.py neutralises the amplitude artefact that the prior campaign's ratio rule was written for).
reviewer_evidence.sd_ratio_meaning: No strength change, KO rep2 noise SD 0.15/0.5/1.0/2.0: genome SD ratio 1.00/0.98/0.935/0.86. After unit scaling the ratio measures replicate concordance (sqrt((1+r_KO)/(1+r_WT))), not compartment strength.
reviewer_evidence.predictor_liftover: 260,534 intervals per track, 984 dropped (0.38%); 551 of 5,776 tiles NaN (480 with zero lifted intervals, 71 with 0 < cov_min < 0.5); NaN tiles are gene-poorer (mean TSS 1.52 vs 3.35) and concentrate on chr9/13/14/15/21/22 (pericentromeric and acrocentric arms); Spearman(cov_min, dlam) = 0.046 and Spearman(cov_min, tss) = 0.15 among all tiles; 27 tiles have cov_min > 1 (max 2.48; multiple hg38 intervals collapsing into one hg19 tile); SD(dlam_mCh) 0.1947; Spearman(tss, dlam) -0.302 as in the hg38 predictor.

blocking.issue: The global confound flag (genome SD(KO PC1)/SD(WT PC1) outside [0.7, 1.4], 'global compartment-strength change present') cannot fire for its stated reason. pc1.compartment_eigenvector scales every chromosome's eigenvector to unit variance per sample, so the evaluator's scale_diagnostic and the standardised arm see tracks whose amplitude carries no strength information. Reviewer simulation: a 1.25x KO amplitude gives ratio 0.997; the ratio drops to 0.86 from KO rep2 noise alone. The flag as written would silently mislabel a replicate-concordance deficit (the half-depth KO rep2 is the likely cause) as a structural change, or miss a real one. The fixed-protocol and registration describe this diagnostic as done and meaningful; it is neither.
blocking.required_repair: Before freeze: (a) add to pc1.py per-chromosome, per-sample compartment-strength statistics that survive scaling, e.g. leading-eigenvalue share lambda1/trace(corr) and lambda1/lambda2, and a saddle-type ratio mean O/E(top-quintile x top-quintile, bottom x bottom) / mean O/E(top x bottom) on the oriented eigenvector; write them to the stats JSON (they are already exposed via pc1_stats in summary.json); (b) pre-state the confound flag on the median per-chromosome KO/WT ratio of one named strength statistic (choose one now; [0.7, 1.4] may be retained) and compute it in replicate.py; (c) relabel the existing genome_sd_ratio as a replicate-concordance diagnostic (reported only) or drop it from the flag; (d) state in the registration that the standardised arm is near-redundant with the unadjusted arm under unit scaling (it adds centring only); (e) add a unit test that the strength statistic detects a planted amplitude change on the block model. No threshold of the pass rule changes.

blocking.issue: Hidden parameters: replicate.run_pc1 invokes pc1.py without --min-abs-rho, --min-nnz or --min-mapq, so pc1.py's argparse defaults (0.2, 10, None) decide per-sample orientation exclusion and ICE masking rather than the registration (orientation.min_rho_per_chromosome, fixed_parameters_explicit.ice_min_nnz). ICE tol=1e-5 and max_iter=200 and the absence of any additional MAPQ filter are not recorded in the registration at all. This is the 'every threshold read fail-closed from the registration' requirement and it is not met for the PC1 stage.
blocking.required_repair: Pass --min-abs-rho reg['orientation']['min_rho_per_chromosome'], --min-nnz reg['fixed_parameters_explicit']['ice_min_nnz'] explicitly in run_pc1 (subscript access, no .get); add fixed_parameters_explicit entries pc1_min_mapq: null ('no filter beyond HiC-Pro valid-pair filtering'), ice_tol: 1e-5, ice_max_iter: 200, eigenvector_scaling: 'unit population SD per chromosome per sample'; add a test asserting the constructed command line contains those values.

blocking.issue: Per-sample orientation failure and cross-sample eigenvector discordance are handled silently. pc1.py orients each sample independently (including KO samples) and writes a chromosome as absent when |rho| < 0.2 in that sample; run_registered's 'finite &=' then removes that chromosome from every statistic without listing it in excluded_chromosomes (orient_tracks records nothing when len(idx) == 0). Nothing checks that a KO sample's leading eigenvector is the same structure as the WT eigenvector; at 500 kb the leading eigenvector can capture arm or centromere structure, and the preprint reports global loop loss and short-range gain in the KO, so a KO chromosome whose eigenvector flips to a non-compartment structure while still clearing |rho| >= 0.2 with TSS density would enter dPC1 as a large structured term. The protocol sentence 'if its PC1 fails orientation on > 2 chromosomes the run still proceeds' is the only pre-statement and it does not say what happens to those chromosomes.
blocking.required_repair: Before freeze: (a) replicate.py reads each sample's stats JSON and lists chromosomes with oriented == false per sample in summary.json as 'dropped_by_per_sample_orientation' (these are dropped from all statistics by construction; say so in the registration); (b) pre-state a per-chromosome concordance rule in the registration and implement it in replicate.py before the evaluator runs: for every sample and chromosome, Spearman(sample PC1, mean WT PC1) over tiles finite in both must be >= 0.5 (WT reps against the other WT rep); a failing chromosome is removed from all four bedGraphs and recorded; (c) pre-state that if more than 3 autosomes are dropped for any reason (orientation, concordance, coverage) the run is reported as PIPELINE_FAILURE and is not a NOT_PASSED outcome; (d) report per-sample genome-wide orientation rho and require >= 0.3 for each WT sample as part of orientation_ok (KO samples reported only); (e) unit tests for (a)-(c) on synthetic bedGraphs.

blocking.issue: The five pre-committed outcomes are not exhaustive in code. replicate.py emits TIER_B_PASS / TIER_A_PASS / OPPOSITE / NOT_PASSED only; the split between 'NOT_PASSED_all_arms_negative_at_floor' and 'NOT_PASSED_otherwise' would be made by hand after outcome access, and the phrase 'p at floor' is ambiguous (p = 1/5001 or p <= 0.01) and 'all arms' does not say whether the four replicate pairs are arms. The prior campaign's report already headlined 'direction as hypothesised in every arm' on a non-pass; without a mechanical definition and a wording rule the same spin is available here.
blocking.required_repair: Define mechanically in the registration and implement in replicate.py with a test: NOT_PASSED_DIRECTION_CONSISTENT iff orientation ok, eligible tiles >= 3000, unadjusted, adjusted and standardised-unadjusted rho all < 0, their three negative-direction p all <= p_max, all four cross replicate pairs negative, and at least one effect floor or the ratio rule unmet; otherwise NOT_PASSED_OTHERWISE. Add to interpretation_precommitted: 'NOT_PASSED_DIRECTION_CONSISTENT carries no evidential weight for the registered claim; the report headline states NOT PASSED; the direction statement may appear only in the body with the effect estimate and the pre-registered power at the floor.' Also state that OPPOSITE is evaluated only when tier A fails (already the code order) so the five labels are disjoint and exhaustive.

blocking.issue: Intake integrity is weaker than described. fixed-protocol.md says 'run refuses on any mismatch', but replicate.check_bindings compares outcome file hashes to intake.json only; intake.py records bytes_match_metadata but nothing refuses on a size mismatch, so a truncated or partial download (intake.py does not clean up partial files) would be hashed as-is and run. GEO publishes no checksums, so bytes_expected is the only external integrity anchor.
blocking.required_repair: In check_bindings, refuse if any intake entry has bytes != reg['outcome']['samples'][gsm]['bytes_expected'] or bytes_match_metadata is not true; in intake.py, delete the partial file and exit non-zero on any exception; add a test for the refusal.

minor.issue: Tier B's -0.10 adjusted floor is anchored to the prior cohort's observed adjusted values (-0.112 / -0.150), not to operating characteristics; that is acceptable for a descriptive effect-size band on top of a tier A pass, but the operating-characteristics section presents it alongside OC-derived numbers. minor.issue: The power statement ('somewhat below the single-arm figure') is unquantified. Reviewer's full-rule simulation (see reviewer_evidence; model assumptions are the reviewer's) gives tier A 5/12 at realised rho -0.048, 12/12 at -0.085; tier B 5/12 at adjusted -0.10; type I 0/12; the four-pairs component alone passes 2/12 under the null. The null-SD file was computed on the hg38 compartment geometry with 2,000 shifts; the KO cohort's null could be wider if the KO dPC1 has arm-level structure, in which case p <= 0.01 becomes the binding constraint (fail-safe).
minor.suggested_repair: Record these figures (with the model caveat) in operating_characteristics and note that the tier A floor -0.05 sits at the null's 0.5th percentile (-0.045 to -0.048), so the effect floor, not p, is binding.

strengths: compartment.py is byte-identical to the compartment campaign's freeze-002 evaluator (hash verified); the adapter maps KO -> 'mutant' and WT -> single corrected line faithfully, copies every tier A threshold by subscript (fail-closed test present), preserves seed 20260925 with the +1/+2/+3 offsets, and replaces the evaluator's two same-index pairs with all four KO-WT cross pairs.

Freeze discipline is sound: freeze.py refuses if any outcome file exists, if this review is not PASS/PASS_WITH_REPAIRS, if method validation is absent or was run on different pc1.py bytes, or if the draft's pc1/test hashes are null or stale; every bound file's bytes are archived; intake happens only after freeze and binds the freeze hash; the run refuses on any hash mismatch.

Unit-variance scaling of the eigenvector per chromosome neutralises the PC1-amplitude artefact that defeated the prior campaign's unadjusted arm in adversarial testing (reviewer: 1.25x KO amplitude gives rho ~0, no component passes).
Full-rule type I error 0/12 in the reviewer's simulation at zero effect; the tier A floor sits at the null's 0.5th percentile so p is never the loophole.

The predictor was built and hash-bound before any outcome access, with a different seed and a different genome build from the prior campaign; liftover loss is small and uncorrelated with the predictor.

Prior-art read is verbatim-quoted, records failed fetches, states the absence of lamin B1 genomic data and of the specific hypothesis, and names the contact-scaling confound before freeze; interpretation of a null as ambiguous between refutation and cardiac specificity is pre-committed.

No contact or endorsement language anywhere; budget and spend consistent; pc1.py is deterministic, documented step by step, and its 26 tests cover binning conventions, ICE masking, O/E, orientation and the pairs/matrix equivalence.
